title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
abstract: arXiv:2610.22312v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spatial instructions describe how to move objects, transform regions, or modify their surroundings. When several operations are applied in sequence, each acts on a configuration shaped by earlier changes. How accurately can large language models (LLMs) predict the resulting spatial state? We introduce Grid-Bench, an executable benchmark in which eight families of operations transform discrete worlds represented as two-, three-, and four-dimensional grids. Given an initial grid, explicit rules, and an event history expressed as text, a model predicts the complete final grid. Reference execution makes every predicted value checkable, supporting comparisons across spatial operations, history lengths, and workloads. Evaluating six LLMs shows that complete-state accuracy falls sharply as histories grow, with substantial divergence among models that perform similarly on single events. translated_title: Grid-Bench：大语言模型能预测离散世界的变化吗？
translated_abstract: 空间指令描述如何移动物体、变换区域或修改其周围环境。当多个操作按顺序应用时，每个操作都作用于由先前变化所塑造的配置。大语言模型（LLM）能够多准确地预测由此产生的空间状态？我们提出了Grid-Bench，这是一个可执行的基准测试，其中八类操作对以二维、三维和四维网格表示的离散世界进行变换。给定一个初始网格、明确的规则以及以文本形式表达的事件历史，模型需要预测完整的最终网格。参考执行机制使得每个预测值都可被检验，从而支持跨空间操作、历史长度和工作负载的比较。对六个大语言模型的评估表明，随着操作历史的增长，完整状态准确率急剧下降，且在单一事件上表现相似的模型之间出现了显著分化。具有相似精确匹配准确率的模型在……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出Grid-Bench——一个可执行的基准测试，用于评估大语言模型在多步空间操作序列下预测离散网格世界完整最终状态的能力，发现随着操作历史增长模型准确率急剧下降且模型间表现差异显著。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Grid-Bench, an executable benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to predict the complete final state of discrete grid worlds under multi-step spatial operation sequences, showing that accuracy drops sharply as history length grows with substantial divergence among models.
